subject: Clarify product rights for R&D outputs and claim language
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jm@ardentbio.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: legal@ardentbio.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on productization/claim language in Order Form redline

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our legal team pushed back on a couple of points that are material for our R&D group and I wanted to get clarification before we escalate to procurement. Main asks below: 

1) Output title / productization: the redline references "perpetual productization rights" for Redwood — can you confirm whether that includes the ability to bundle outputs into a commercial model or product that would be sold to third parties? Our concern is downstream use that would allow Redwood to claim ownership of derivatives created from our confidential prompts and outputs.

2) Training / model re-use: we need an explicit commitment that customer-provided content (prompts, files, outputs flagged as confidential) will not be used to retrain or improve model weights outside of telemetry/operational metrics. Is there a standard carveout for R&D code and proprietary data?

3) Feedback/telemetry license: your order form asks for a broad feedback license — can we get language that limits feedback to service improvement only (no model redistribution or productization)?

Attached: our redlines on the order form for reference (comments inline). If it helps, can we set a short call with your legal lead and technical product to run through examples?

Appreciate the help — Jordan

[Attachment: ArdentBio_OrderForm_Redline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jm@ardentbio.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 14:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on productization/claim language in Order Form redline

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping in our legal lead (Laura) and product ops (Rishi, Grace) to get a definitive response. Quick high-level before legal weighs in:

- Redwood is not seeking exclusive ownership of customer outputs. We typically grant customers broad use rights for outputs and productization for their own offerings, and we avoid asserting ownership of customer-specific outputs.
- On retraining: our standard approach is to exclude customer-provided proprietary content from model retraining unless the customer opts in (we call this a "training opt-in"). We can add explicit exclusion language for R&D artifacts.
- Feedback license: we can narrow the feedback license to "service improvement" and telemetry; we will propose language that prohibits model redistribution or selling derivatives that incorporate identifiable customer content.

Action items:
1) Laura — can you propose specific counterlanguage we can share with ArdentBio?
2) Rishi/Grace — any technical constraints we should flag (e.g., telemetry windows, retention limits, redaction)?
3) Jordan — are you available Mon/Tue next week for a 30-min sync?

Thanks — Stephanie

--

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 4 May 2028 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: FW: Clarification on productization/claim language in Order Form redline — proposed language

Team — drafting notes and proposed text we can offer ArdentBio. Below are the tradeoffs and a recommended compromise to move the deal without creating undue IP exposure: 

Recommended counter (high level):
- Output ownership: Insert express language that "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Content and Outputs generated by the Service that are identified in writing as Customer Confidential Information; Redwood receives no ownership rights in such Customer Outputs." This protects R&D artifacts while leaving typical outputs free for customer use.

- Training / re-use carveout: Add an opt-in clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or improve its models for general distribution without the Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and service metrics (non-identifying) to monitor and improve service performance."

- Feedback license narrow scope: Replace broad feedback license with: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Customer feedback solely to improve, operate, and maintain the Redwood Service; such license does not permit commingling customer-specific content into model training datasets for commercial models."

Operational considerations (Rishi/Grace): propose explicit retention and deletion windows for telemetry (e.g., 90 days for request-level logs unless retained for debugging with customer consent), and an obvious opt-out path. Also flag that limited prefix caching for latency is separate from model training and must be covered in docs.

Attachment: I prepared a tracked-changes counter-redline with the three clauses above. If we accept those terms we should be able to preserve our ability to improve the service while giving ArdentBio the carveouts they want for R&D data.

Proposed next step: Stephanie to share the tracked redline and a one-paragraph summary to ArdentBio, and propose a 30-minute legal+tech call.

Best,
Laura

[Attachment: proposed_counter_redline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jm@ardentbio.com>
Cc: ArdentBio Legal <legal@ardentbio.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 May 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on productization/claim language in Order Form redline

Jordan — following internal review, attached is a concise counterproposal and the tracked order form with the clauses Laura suggested. High-level summary below so your legal team doesn't need to parse the whole doc: 

1) Customer outputs: expressly retained by Customer; Redwood will not claim ownership of outputs flagged as Customer Confidential Information.
2) Training opt-in: Redwood will only use Customer Content or Outputs to train models with prior written consent; telemetry/operational metrics for service improvements are permitted and will be aggregated and non-identifying.
3) Feedback license: limited to service improvement; does not allow model redistribution or commingling into general training datasets.

We also propose standard telemetry retention (90 days) and an option for ArdentBio to request artifact deletion for specific request traces within 30 days. If this aligns with ArdentBio's expectations we can update the order form and route to DocuSign. I linked the draft in HubSpot and prepared a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789012 (Deal RBW-2028-074) — DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/abcd1234

If you want to run through two short examples (1 — customer provides proprietary sequences that should never be reused; 2 — anonymized usage metrics for latency improvement), Rishi and Grace are available on Wed afternoon.

Thanks,
Stephanie
